text.arabic_uthmani: وَلَنُذِيقَنَّهُم مِّنَ ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلْأَدْنَىٰ دُونَ ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلْأَكْبَرِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ

baseline.text: Belki dönerler diye onlara büyük azaptan önce daha yakın azaptan mutlaka tattıracağız.

findings.text: Yakın ve büyük azap, aynı şeyin iki adı değil, ilk tecrübenin büyük sonucun bu yanında kaldığı ve hâlâ ders verebildiği aşamalı bir ölçektir.
Yakın azabın tattırılması, kişiye gittiği yönü sonucu kesinleşmeden deneyimletip önceki yolundan dönme imkânı veren düzeltici bir sınamadır.
Yakınlık, inkâr edilen geleceğin sınırlı bir örneğini kullanılabilir bugünkü kanıta çevirir; değeri, tepkinin hâlâ sonucu değiştirebildiği zamanda gelmesidir.

activation_trace.role: Experience and trial make the punishment personally knowable and let it function as an embodied warning.
Inflicted pain supplies the literal punitive material whose two occurrences are graded.
The nearer, smaller, or first tier locates this punishment within reach and before another.
Being short of the endpoint bounds the first ordeal below the greater one.
Magnitude supplies the terminal contrast that makes the nearer tier comparatively limited.
Turning away from an offense supplies the corrective response toward which the ordeal is directed.

changed_reading.after: A deliberately experienced nearer ordeal is a bounded warning sample, kept short of the greater punishment so that reversal remains possible.
changed_reading.before: A smaller punishment simply precedes a larger punishment.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The causative tasting, the nearer/below/greater grading, and the purpose clause ending in return.
baseline_models.mechanism: Punishment is made personally knowable as an ordeal, but proximity and the boundary short of the greater punishment limit that ordeal; its open purpose is corrective reversal rather than arrival at the terminal tier.

activation_trace.role: The repeated punishment noun supplies two punitive terms available for comparison.
Nearer, smaller, or first preserves the obvious scalar ordering.
Otherness opens a second relation in which the nearer punishment is distinct from the greater one.
Greater magnitude maintains the competing degree-based reading rather than allowing category alone to settle the phrase.

changed_reading.after: The nearer punishment is certainly ordered below the greater, yet may also be another category of consequence rather than merely a diluted copy.
changed_reading.before: The two punishments differ only by severity.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The combination of the nearer punishment, dūna, and the greater punishment.
baseline_models.mechanism: The nearer adjective establishes a scalar relation, while the other-than branch of dūna keeps a categorical relation alive; the two punishments can differ in kind as well as degree.

activation_trace.role: Literal oral tasting supplies the intake image against which deprivation becomes perceptible.
Abstention from food or drink turns punishment into an experience of not receiving what is sought.
Withholding and weaning provide the corrective mechanism of forced detachment.
Turning away from the prior course supplies the hoped result of that detachment.

changed_reading.after: One exploratory mode of nearer punishment is deprivation or weaning: absence itself is made felt so that attachment may break and return may begin.
changed_reading.before: Punishment is only pain positively imposed.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The lexical collision between tasting and the two punishment nouns, followed by hoped-for return.
baseline_models.mechanism: Tasting normally implies intake, while branches of the punishment root include not eating or drinking and active withholding or weaning; this permits a near punishment felt as denied access or forced detachment, meant to loosen a harmful attachment and provoke return.

activation_trace.role: A warning that awakens caution supplies the earlier communicative stage of the corrective mechanism.
Gentle direction toward a path supplies the hoped outcome parallel to return.
Experienced ordeal converts warning from heard information into personally known consequence.
Turning from the offense gives the later purpose clause its corrective destination.

changed_reading.after: It participates in a warning system: consequence itself communicates when warning speech has not yet produced guided return.
changed_reading.before: The nearer punishment is a reduced penalty with an incidental hope of repentance.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier warning-to-guidance sequence makes the nearer punishment an embodied continuation of warning: speech alerts, experienced consequence makes the alert tangible, and both remain directed toward a recoverable response.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies warning followed by hoped-for guidance in 32:3 and tasting followed by hoped-for return in 32:21; I infer a functional progression from verbal alert to embodied alert, while the live alternative is simple thematic parallel without a staged process.
structural_cues: 32:3 and 32:21 both close with laʿallahum purpose clauses, first hoping for guidance and later for return.

activation_trace.role: A relation of otherness distinguishes alternative protectors from God and establishes a nearby non-scalar use.
The same otherness branch lets the nearer punishment be distinct from the greater punishment.
The short-of-the-goal sense keeps the scalar reading active beside categorical distinction.

changed_reading.after: The first punishment may be both lower and other than the greater one, allowing worldly or otherwise distinct consequences without identifying any one instance.
changed_reading.before: Dūna only says that the first punishment is less severe.

context_deltas.mechanism: The packet has already used dūn to separate God from alternative protectors and intercessors, so its other-than force remains locally active when it later separates the nearer punishment from the greater one.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a nearby other-than use; I carry that semantic availability into 32:21, but not its exact syntax. The live alternative is that the nearer/greater adjectives force a purely scalar relation in the focus.
structural_cues: In 32:4 dūn mediates an exclusive relational contrast; in 32:21 it stands directly between the two punishment phrases.

activation_trace.role: Return to an originating destination supplies the inevitable terminal movement toward the Lord.
Requested restoration to a prior arena supplies the too-late desire for another chance to act.
Actual seeing marks the point at which denied consequence has become undeniable perception.
Hearing as understanding or compliance marks recognition that arrives after the actionable interval.
Turning from the offense identifies the return still sought while correction can matter.

changed_reading.after: They are given an experiential interval in which moral return can precede inevitable return; after full disclosure, asking to return for action is no substitute.

context_deltas.mechanism: Three return positions separate: inevitable return to the Lord, a later plea to be sent back for righteous action after perception is certain, and the focus's hoped moral return under nearer punishment. The focus is therefore a pre-terminal opportunity, not generic motion backward.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies three return constructions at different moments; I infer that 32:21 occupies the still-actionable interval before the requested return of 32:12, while the live alternative is that its return also broadly anticipates return to God.
structural_cues: 32:11 announces return to the Lord; 32:12 immediately voices a plea to be returned for righteous action after seeing and hearing.

activation_trace.role: Repeated made-experience shows that tasting can intensify certainty without implying a temporary sample.
Literal punitive pain supplies the consequence paired with enduring duration.
Loss of remembrance supplies the opposite trajectory to the focus's hoped return.
Persistence without quick ending closes the temporary corrective interval.
Nearer or first supplies the bounded temporal and scalar qualification absent from the abiding punishment.
Turning from the offense supplies the focus-specific remedial aim.

changed_reading.after: Tasting means made experience and can be either provisional or abiding; only 32:21's grading and return-purpose create a corrective window.
changed_reading.before: To taste punishment means to receive a small corrective sample.

context_deltas.mechanism: The same tasting idiom can carry an abiding punishment tied to forgetting, so tasting itself does not make punishment remedial. In the focus, correction arises from the nearer/below grading and the purpose of return; in 32:14, persistence and failed remembrance close that function.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies shared tasting language but opposed duration and response frames; I infer that frame, not the sensory verb alone, determines whether punishment remains corrective. The alternative is that both passages merely emphasize direct experience without a designed contrast.
structural_cues: 32:14 repeats the tasting command and connects enduring punishment to forgetting the encounter, whereas 32:21 subordinates tasting to possible return.

activation_trace.role: Movement to the outside supplies the attempted escape that initiates the loop.
Return after departure supplies forced reinstatement inside the punishment.
Made experience binds the closed return loop to the same sensory mode used in the focus.
Punitive pain is the location into which attempted escape is reversed.
Turning from the offense supplies the voluntary opposite of forced return into punishment.

changed_reading.after: They also differ in mobility: the nearer punishment can redirect a person out of a course, while the greater punishment encloses attempted exit in compulsory return.
changed_reading.before: Lesser punishment and greater punishment differ mainly in intensity.

context_deltas.mechanism: Immediately before the focus, attempted exit from fire produces forced return into it; in the focus, tasted punishment is meant to produce return away from the prior course. The same return topology is inverted: the nearer tier still has an open corrective exit, while the greater tier is a closed punitive loop.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adjacent forced and hoped returns under shared tasting language; I infer a deliberate topological reversal, while the live alternative is that adjacency contrasts only degrees of punishment, not two kinds of return.
structural_cues: 32:20 repeats an attempted-exit and forced-return cycle, then 32:21 immediately presents punishment with the hope of a different return.

activation_trace.role: A reminder supplies the renewed intervention to which a response is required.
Turning one's side away supplies the failed response that moves opposite to return.
Punishment following rejection supplies the consequence when the corrective opening is refused.
Turning away from the offense remains the hoped but non-compulsory response.

changed_reading.after: It creates a corrective interruption whose purpose can fail; the subject may turn away from the intervention instead of turning back from the offense.
changed_reading.before: The nearer punishment reliably causes return.

context_deltas.mechanism: Reminder can be answered by bodily and attentional turning-away rather than return, followed by punishment after rejection. The focus therefore states an aim and opportunity, not a guaranteed causal result.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a failed reminder-response sequence immediately after the focus; I infer it as a live failure branch for the focus's purpose clause, while the alternative is that 32:22 introduces a different population rather than the same response logic.
structural_cues: 32:22 follows the focus with a reminder, then deliberate turning-away, then punitive consequence.

activation_trace.role: Oral tasting anchors the exploratory mechanism in bodily intake.
Not eating or drinking provides the felt deprivation at the end of an interrupted supply chain.
Withholding supplies the possible punitive operation without replacing the ordinary pain sense.
Driving supplies the active conveyance of water that enables the downstream material sequence.
Land cut off from vegetation supplies the deprived state that the arriving water reverses.
Growth supplies the intermediate conversion of water into nourishment.
Eating supplies the terminal intake whose absence would be bodily experienced.

changed_reading.after: They gain an exploratory material mechanism: nearer punishment could be felt where the water-to-food chain is withheld or broken, making absence itself something tasted.
changed_reading.before: The deprivation branches are an isolated lexical curiosity.

context_deltas.mechanism: The packet's material chain moves water into vegetation-cut land, produces crop, and ends in eating. Read in reverse as an explicitly reader-supplied counterfactual, interruption of that chain gives concrete content to the focus-only deprivation and weaning model: a punishment tasted through absent intake.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the positive restoration chain; I infer its interruption or withdrawal as a possible concrete form of deprivation, while the materially live alternative is that 32:27 is only a provision sign and does not specify any punishment in 32:21.
structural_cues: 32:27 orders a visible chain from conveyed water through bare land and crop to eating by livestock and people.

activation_trace.role: An opening that begins what follows supplies the threshold whose timing is demanded.
Judicial opening supplies the decisive event that closes the earlier corrective interval.
The explicit loss of benefit marks a response that has become ineffective.
Belief as settled assent supplies the response that no longer changes the outcome after the threshold.
Withheld delay removes any additional interval for response.
Remaining short of the endpoint locates the nearer punishment before that closure.
Turning from the offense supplies the response that can still matter before the threshold.

changed_reading.after: They also mark two sides of a deadline: nearer punishment still addresses a changeable subject, while beyond the opening neither late assent nor more time alters the outcome.
changed_reading.before: Nearer and greater describe only a severity ladder.

context_deltas.mechanism: The asked-for opening becomes a judgment threshold after which faith brings no benefit and no further delay is granted. This gives the nearer punishment a temporal function: it occurs on the actionable side of a deadline, whereas the greater punishment belongs beyond recoverability.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an explicit no-benefit and no-delay threshold; I infer that 32:21's hoped-for return belongs before it, while the live alternative is that the greater punishment and the day of opening overlap only partially.
structural_cues: 32:28 asks when the opening will occur; 32:29 answers that at its arrival belief will not benefit and delay will not be given.

remaining_uncertainties: The nearer/greater syntax may dominate dūna's other-than branch and reduce the category distinction to a secondary resonance.
The packet does not identify which concrete events instantiate the nearer punishment.
The ecological deprivation model depends on reversing a positive provision chain and therefore remains exploratory.
The bow-test and ruins readings are analogical activations, not lexical glosses.
strongest_changes: The nearer punishment became an actionable warning interval rather than merely a weaker penalty.
Return split into voluntary moral reversal, inevitable return to the Lord, a too-late request to be sent back, and forced return into fire.
Dūna preserved a distinct-category reading alongside the scalar contrast.
Tasting proved neutral between provisional and abiding punishment; duration and purpose determine its function.
The deprivation branches gained an exploratory water-to-food mechanism without displacing the ordinary punishment sense.
summary.what_was_special: The focus concentrates two punishment nouns between sensory experience, a doubled proximity boundary, and return; nearby context then inverts return, closes its deadline, and gives odd deprivation branches a material ecology.

activation_trace.role: Testing a bow under tension supplies a bounded stress that reveals response before full strain.
Stopping short of the endpoint limits the applied stress.
Greater heaviness supplies the fuller strain that the nearer test precedes.
Recoil or return supplies the observable directional response to limited pressure.

changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, it is calibrated pressure that discloses whether a return response remains possible before the heavier endpoint.
changed_reading.before: The lesser punishment is simply a lower dose.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it transfers the branch image of testing a bow into the punitive sequence; it remains anchored in causative tasting and the near/below/greater grading, but downstream prose should present it only as a material analogy for calibrated pressure, never as a lexical translation or settled intent.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Causative tasting bounded by the nearer, below, and greater construction.

activation_trace.role: Experience and trial allow consequence to become known through material encounter.
Proximity lets another generation's consequence become a near and traversable warning.
Destruction and perishing supply the prior consequence whose residue remains available.
Bodily movement supplies direct traversal rather than detached information.
Formerly inhabited places supply the material setting in which prior destruction is encountered.
Hearing as understanding or compliance supplies the corrective response sought from that encounter.

changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, its warning function can include bodily encounter with nearby residues of prior destruction, making consequence present before one's own terminal return.
changed_reading.before: The nearer punishment must directly strike the addressed people.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it reads punishment through encountered remains rather than direct injury; it stays anchored in tasting as experienced ordeal and proximity, while 32:26 supplies walking and responsive hearing amid destroyed dwellings. Downstream prose should qualify it as an experiential analogy, not identify the nearer punishment exclusively with ruins.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Tasting as lived experience and the description of punishment as nearer.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Near punishment before the greater threshold.** **د ن و B001-B002** supplies nearness and the nearer or first side; **د و ن B001** supplies what is near yet short of a limit; **ك ب ر B001-B002** supplies the greater scale and chief burden. The two punishments are ordered by distance and magnitude, and the purpose clause remains open. I infer that the nearer experience occurs on the still-reversible side of a threshold. الأدنى therefore reads temporally and functionally as an advance intervention, not only a smaller quantity of pain.
2. **Punishment as diagnostic testing.** **ذ و ق B002** supplies experiencing and testing; **ع ذ ب B005** supplies punishment; **ر ج ع B003** supplies turning back from an act or prior course. The explicit لَعَلَّهُمْ supplies the desired direction. I infer that this taste reveals the trajectory early enough to prompt reversal. The painful experience has a corrective function distinct from the closed recurrence of 32:20.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The reminder followed by turning away in 32:22 showed how the corrective opening can be refused. The final opening in 32:29, when faith no longer benefits and no respite is granted, later fixed the far boundary implied by **دُونَ** here.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **The two punishments form a scale rather than synonyms.** `د ن و:B002` directly covers *al-adnā* as the nearer, lower, smaller, or first side; `ك ب ر:B001` supplies greatness for *al-akbar*. The partitive *min* and `د و ن:B001`, below or short of a limit, place the first experience on this side of the greater one. **Packet relation:** some nearer punishment precedes and falls short of the greater punishment. **Inferred arrow:** differentiated scale -> an interval in which consequence can still instruct.

2. **The stated purpose is corrective return.** `ذ و ق:B002` gives direct undergoing, and `ر ج ع:B003` specifically supplies turning back from sin or a prior course. *Laʿallahum yarjiʿūn* makes return the disclosed aim of the nearer tasting. **Packet arrow:** nearer experienced consequence -> possible turning back. This changes punishment from undifferentiated retribution into a diagnostic intervention whose success would be altered orientation.

3. **Proximity converts a denied future into usable present evidence.** The emphatic *la-nudhīqannahum* guarantees an experience, while *al-adnā* locates it before the greater endpoint. In 32:20, `ك ذ ب:B002` named denial and `ذ و ق:B002` named terminal experience; in 32:22, reminder will again precede a choice of orientation. **Inferred arrow:** a limited present contact with consequence -> interruption of denial -> renewed opportunity to face the reminder. The nearer punishment is meaningful precisely because it arrives while response remains causally effective.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 32:22 showed why the purpose clause is only prospective, not guaranteed: after reminder, a person can still turn his side away. 32:26 then made destroyed generations another nearer warning, so the corrective tasting in 32:21 belongs to a wider sequence of interventions whose efficacy depends on response.

words.gloss_range: connective and resumptive opening that carries the prior punishment scene into a new sworn declaration
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) does more than add another clause; it carries the fire-scene boundary from 32:20 into a fresh first-person declaration. Because it is prefixed into the same opening unit as the emphatic particle and the causative verb, the transition feels compressed: continuity, resumption, and sworn certainty enter together before the punishment is named. Its clipped opening rushes into the heavy verbal form rather than lingering as a detachable connector.

topics.headline: boundary resumption into declaration
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 32:21 continues the punishment scene of 32:20 while shifting into a new direct divine undertaking.
topics.reason: The opening conjunction begins the main verbal assertion and the boundary rows connect it to 32:20 rather than treating it as an isolated threat.

topics.headline: connective fused into emphatic onset
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the connective enter the same compressed unit as the oath-colored certainty, so connection and force are not separate effects.
topics.reason: The particle is prefixed to the emphatic verbal complex, and the following particle plus energetic ending carry qasam force.

topics.headline: clipped rush into the verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the short prefixed opening rushing into the heavy verbal form, matching the ayah's forceful launch.
topics.reason: The sound row is local to the prefixed onset and supports the same compressed opening already visible in the morphology.

words.gloss_range: emphatic oath particle prefixed to the imperfect verb, making the whole verbal assertion settled rather than merely future
words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) turns the coming verb phrase into an oath-colored assertion. Its force reaches across the whole making-taste event, including the affected group and the partitive punishment phrase. Since the certainty is carried as a prefix and answered by the heavy energetic ending on {{ar:نُذِيقَنَّهُمْ}} ({{tr:nudhīqannahum}}), the grammar makes the imposed tasting settled while the later return remains grammatically open.

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: emphatic causative verb whose heavy ending answers the prefixed particle

topics.headline: oath force over the assertion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the particle gives settled assertional force to the whole making-taste event, not just to the first syllable of the verb.
topics.reason: QAC and translation support identify the prefixed particle as emphatic and tied to the finite verbal assertion.

topics.headline: front particle answered by heavy ending
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees certainty distributed through the verbal form from prefixed particle to energetic closure.
topics.reason: The local verb has both the prefixed emphatic particle and the heavy energetic ending.

topics.headline: first beat launched under certainty
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the first beat start under certainty before the ayah explains the measure, limit, and purpose of what is sworn.
topics.reason: The particle stands at the opening of the main assertion and is phonologically bound to the verb complex.

words.gloss_range: Form IV causative making-taste: imposed sensory experience with direct object suffix and partitive punishment complement
words.prose: {{ar:نُذِيقَنَّهُمْ}} ({{tr:nudhīqannahum}}) gathers divine agency, certainty, and the affected group into one form: We will surely make them taste. The Form IV shape makes the experience imposed rather than self-initiated, while the object suffix makes the prior guilty group the direct patients. The taste root keeps punishment as contact-based perception, not a distant announcement, and the partitive complement that follows makes the tasted thing a measured portion of punishment. Against {{ar:ذُوقُوا}} ({{tr:dhūqū}}) in 32:20, the same root shifts from a command addressed to the condemned into a sworn divine undertaking.
words.root_gloss_range: tasting, firsthand experience, perception, and discernment; here selected through Form IV causative punishment experience rather than autonomous tasting

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: imperative taste form from 32:20 contrasted with the local first-person causative

topics.headline: imposed sensory experience
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the subjects do not merely taste; they are made to taste, so corrective experience is externally administered.
topics.reason: The aligned form is Form IV with a direct object suffix and a partitive complement, supporting causative making-taste.

topics.headline: certainty, speaker, and patients compressed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the divine speaker, the affected group, and future certainty arrive before the punishment noun itself is named.
topics.reason: The verb carries first-person plural subject agreement, heavy energetic ending, and the 3mp object suffix.

topics.headline: object separated from tasted portion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the argument frame: they are the patients, while punishment is the portion or source they are made to experience.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the suffix as object and the following prepositional phrase as the punishment complement.

topics.headline: punishment as contact-based perception
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the punishment as firsthand perception and corrective data, not only as a legal consequence.
topics.reason: The root's tasting and experiential-knowing range is locally selected by the punishment-tasting construction.

topics.headline: command becomes divine undertaking
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the root return from the imperative command in 32:20 to a first-person causative act in 32:21.

words.prose: {{ar:يَرْجِعُونَ}} ({{tr:yarjiʿūna}}) closes the ayah on possible response rather than on punishment. It is active and intransitive here, so the same group must themselves return instead of being forced back or returning an object. Because no destination is named, the return remains broad: turning back, reforming, and redirecting course all remain available under the local purpose clause. The imperfect form lacks the energetic certainty of {{ar:نُذِيقَنَّهُمْ}} ({{tr:nudhīqannahum}}), so the ayah contrasts a certain imposed taste with an open human return. The corrective-return formula also recurs where consequence or testing aims at return (6:42, 7:168, 43:28, 46:27). Against the forced return loop in 32:20 and related return language in 32:11 and 32:12, this final verb offers a hoped voluntary reversal.
